help:
Drive a real screen and record the result as a c:test_run entity with its screenshots attached.

web: Chromium (Chrome for Testing 156) in a gVisor sandbox on the tm8 host, driven by callstack's agent-device. --profiles desktop,iphone,pixel sets viewport and user agent; iphone and pixel are Chromium at that size, not the phone.
android, ios: a real emulator or simulator from a device cloud (--provider limrun with the limrun_api_key secret) or behind an agent-device proxy (--provider proxy, --proxy-url and the proxy_token secret). Without one the run is recorded as blocked, with the evidence, never faked.

Example: tm8 tool run device-test --target https://tm8-hub.com/ --expect-text "one live graph" --profiles desktop,iphone,pixel --task <task-id>

Exit status: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 error (the harness, not the product), 3 blocked, 64 bad arguments; a batch exits with its worst result. See tools/device-test/README.md.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The http(s) URL to open. For android or ios with a --suite, it can be the app id the suite opens.

inputs.name: platform
inputs.description: web runs here; android and ios need a --provider.

inputs.name: expect_text
inputs.description: Text the screen must show. The run fails, keeping the screenshot it failed on, if the text does not appear.

inputs.name: profiles
inputs.description: Web only, comma-separated: desktop (1280x900), iphone (390x844), pixel (412x915). One run each.

inputs.name: suite
inputs.description: An agent-device .ad replay script to run instead of the built-in check. Must be inside your working directory or a path grant.

inputs.name: app
inputs.description: android and ios with a --suite: an .apk, .app, .ipa or .zip, mounted read-only as ${APP} for the suite to install.

inputs.name: allow_domains
inputs.description: Web only: more domains the page may load from, comma-separated (*.example.com allowed). The target's own domain is always allowed; everything else is refused.

inputs.name: network
inputs.description: host lets the browser reach services on this machine (127.0.0.1); bridge does not. host needs sandbox runc.

inputs.name: sandbox
inputs.description: gvisor gives each container a kernel of its own, so a browser exploit meets gVisor, not the host's kernel. runc is Docker's default runtime, with a seccomp profile for Chrome.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: android and ios: where the device runs.

inputs.name: proxy_url
inputs.description: --provider proxy: the agent-device proxy base URL. Its token is the proxy_token secret.

inputs.name: task
inputs.description: A task to relate each run to and to post the verdict on, with the screenshots attached.

inputs.name: run
inputs.description: Record the first run into this existing c:test_run, such as one queued from the UI, instead of creating one.

inputs.name: revision
inputs.description: The build of the target under test, recorded on each run.

inputs.name: timeout
inputs.description: Seconds per run. Default 300 for web, 900 for a device. tm8 stops the whole tool run after 3600.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: An existing directory for screenshots, logs and report.json. Default: this tool run's own directory.

inputs.name: record
inputs.description: Write runs to tm8. --no-record keeps everything in the output directory.

inputs.name: limrun_api_key
inputs.description: Limrun API key: agent-device creates a device for the run and deletes it when the run lets it go. If the run dies first, Limrun's inactivity timeout ends it.

inputs.name: limrun_region
inputs.description: Optional Limrun region for new devices.

inputs.name: lim_android_instance_url
inputs.description: Use an Android instance you created yourself; needs all three LIM_ANDROID_INSTANCE inputs. agent-device never creates or deletes it.

inputs.name: lim_android_instance_token
inputs.description: The token of that Android instance.

inputs.name: lim_android_instance_adb_url
inputs.description: The adb URL of that Android instance.

inputs.name: lim_ios_instance_url
inputs.description: Use an iOS instance you created yourself; needs both LIM_IOS_INSTANCE inputs.

inputs.name: lim_ios_instance_token
inputs.description: The token of that iOS instance.

inputs.name: proxy_token
inputs.description: --provider proxy: the agent-device proxy's bearer token.
